Suites: src/. Each *-list file is the stdout of that runner's list command
(*-units files, added 2026-10-25 on node v22.23.4: the unit listing under
its working-directory prelude, the capture directory written as /fixture)
(jest and mocha JSON reduced to the fields the parsers read).
Each *-fail, *-suitefail, *-loadfail and *-hookfail file is stdout+stderr of
the runner's DEFAULT command on src/fail, not a TTY, as the jail runs it;
minitest 5.20.0.

gotestsum 1.13.0 (go install), PHP 8.5.4,

*-help files are each runner's --help; libtest-help.txt is a cargo-built test binary's.
cargo-units-jail.txt (added 2026-10-25, cargo 1.90.0): the cargo-units.txt
listing from a clean target dir with stderr on the same stream, as the jail
returns a run's output; cargo's Compiling/Finished lines sit between its
JSON messages.
*-units-multi*.txt (added 2026-10-27; jest 30.5.2, vitest 3.2.7, node v22.23.4,
rspec-core 3.13.6, PHPUnit 11.5.57, go1.26.10, gotestsum 1.13.0, cargo 1.90.0,
cargo-nextest 0.9.148): each row's multi-unit command for units a and b of
three (src/units/multi; Go's units/gomod under -tags extra; the cargo
workspace), as "# argv:" the operator's command, "$ " the command run, then
its stdout+stderr with timings and run ids removed. Run with the agent
variables unset: jest 30 prints only its summary when it sees one.
vitest5-fail.txt, vitest5-fail-projects.txt and vitest5-fail-projects-nocolor.txt
(added 2026-10-31, vitest 5.0.3 on node v24.22.1, captured by hand, not by
the script): the default command on src/fail-vitest5 under `env -i` (PATH,
HOME, LANG only, as the jail sets them), not a TTY; -projects with
vitest.projects.config.mjs as vitest.config.mjs, -nocolor with NO_COLOR=1.
vitest 5 colours its output with no TTY and no colour variable, which is
how a jailed run returns it; $DIR, ms timings, start time and duration
replaced.

vitest 5.1.0 and mocha 12.0.3 (jest unchanged at 30.5.2), node v22.23.5,
go1.26.11, cargo 1.90.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.148, rspec-core 3.13.6, PHPUnit

swift-*.txt and toolchain-swift-version.txt (added 2026-11-19; Swift version 6.3.2 (swift-6.3.2-RELEASE),
Target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu): scripts/capture-runner-fixtures.sh
through a container of corral-swift-spike run as the invoking user, on src/swift, whose test targets are CalcTests (swift-testing, five tests) and
CalcXCTests (XCTest, three, in class AdderTests). swift-list.txt is the stdout
of `swift test list`; swift-units.txt the stdout of `swift package describe
--type json` under the unit-listing prelude, the capture directory written as
/fixture; every other file is stdout+stderr, not a TTY, with the capture
directory written as $DIR. swift-fail-testing.txt and swift-fail-xctest.txt
are `swift test` with CORRAL_FAIL_TESTING or CORRAL_FAIL_XCTEST set, which
the fixture reads to plant its failures; swift-build-fail.txt is `swift test`
after a line that does not compile was appended to Sources/Calc/Calc.swift.
swift-build-target-*.txt are the compile check's `swift build --target`:
of a test target, of the source target, of a test target while a sibling
test target did not compile (with a scratch path of its own), and of a test
target after a line that does not compile was appended to the source.
swift-authored-wrapped.txt runs the two files under
src/swift-authored/wrapped, copied into the test targets, and
swift-authored-collision.txt builds CalcTests with
src/swift-authored/collision's file copied into it. swift-shapes-list.txt is
the stdout of `swift test list` with src/swift-authored/shapes's file copied
into CalcTests.
swift-single-*.txt, swift-filter-dollar.txt, swift-units-*.txt,
swift-build-target-*.txt and swift-authored-*.txt open with
`# argv:` (the operator's command, `-` for corral's own compile check)
and `$ ` (the command corral builds) and end with `# exit:` (its exit status). swift-testing runs its tests in
parallel, so the order of its lines differs between captures.
The swift-build-target-*.txt, swift-authored-*.txt and
swift-shapes-list.txt files come from a later --swift-only run of the same
script on the same toolchain (2026-11-19); that run's other Swift captures
were not kept, because swift-testing's parallel order differs between runs
and the committed ones are what the tests were written against.
